title: Work Statistics Under Quantum-Jump and Quench Dynamics in Monitored Ising Chains
abstract: We investigate work statistics in monitored transverse-field Ising chains subject to both a quantum quench of the transverse field and either stochastic quantum jumps or controlled measurement sequences. For generalized measurements, we derive a trajectory-resolved generating function for work statistics in the two-point energy measurement scheme. Evaluating it using a fermionic Gaussian-state formalism, we show that, under stochastic jump dynamics, the work distribution crosses over from a comb-like structure to an essentially Gaussian form with shrinking sub-Gaussian tails, as the number of detection events grows. For controlled jump protocols, the energy added by each jump is constant when successive jumps are causally disconnected but decreases and then saturates when they lie within each other's light cone, yielding linear and sublinear growth of the average work, respectively. For monitored quenches, continuous observation washes out the fine structure of the isolated-quench distribution and again drives the statistics toward Gaussian behavior.
summary: This paper analyzes the statistics of work done on monitored Ising chains under quantum quenches and stochastic measurements. It demonstrates that frequent monitoring drives the system's work distribution towards Gaussian behavior, while controlled jumps reveal distinct linear versus sublinear growth rates based on causal correlations. This offers deep insights into how measurement backaction shapes non-equilibrium thermodynamics.
main_problem: The study investigates how work statistics evolve in monitored quantum systems subjected to both quantum quenches and continuous measurement processes.
main_result: Frequent monitoring drives the work distribution towards an essentially Gaussian form, while controlled measurements reveal distinct growth regimes depending on whether energy increments are causally disconnected or correlated within a light cone.
method: The analysis employs deriving trajectory-resolved generating functions for work statistics and evaluating them using fermionic Gaussian-state formalisms.
model_or_system: The system is the transverse-field Ising chain, whose dynamics are governed by stochastic quantum jumps (unraveling of a Lindblad master equation) or controlled deterministic projections.
key_observables: Work distribution P(W), work generating function G(u), mean work <W>, and variance σ²_W.
important_parameters: Measurement rate (γ), number of detection events, transverse field strength (h), and the causal separation between measurement jumps (inside/outside light cone).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Central Limit Theorem to explain the approach to Gaussianity for large numbers of weakly correlated increments.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the transition of P(W) from discrete peaks to Gaussian shapes as monitoring strength increases, and compare work statistics under isolated quenches versus monitored dynamics.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes work statistics across different measurement protocols: stochastic jumps (showing crossover), controlled deterministic jumps (highlighting causality effects), and the combined effect of quenching with continuous observation.
why_interesting: It provides a quantitative framework for understanding how measurement backaction fundamentally alters non-equilibrium thermodynamics, moving beyond simple average energy calculations to characterize fluctuations in work.
